subject: Private deployment: environment governance & access pledge
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novothera.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Infra Team <infra-owner@novothera.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Environment governance & access pledge for private deployment

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare for the VPC/private deployment, our security/compliance team asked us to collect a clear governance and access pledge from Redwood that covers: network connectivity responsibilities, KMS ownership and key residency, emergency access procedures, and logging/retention commitments.

Attached is a short template the compliance team uses — would you be able to confirm which items Redwood will own vs. what NovoThera needs to provide? We need the completed pledge before our legal and InfoSec signoff.

Key dates: we hope to have signoff by 2028-08-10 to keep the cutover window.

Attachments: governance-template.pdf (PDF, 240KB)

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Head of Infrastructure Programs
NovoThera Medical
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novothera.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment governance & access pledge for private deployment

Maria — thanks for the template and the clear timeline. We can take the lead on most of the operational governance items; below is a concise mapping and next steps. I attached a draft pledge (redwood-pledge-draft.docx) for you to review and a short networking prerequisites note.

High-level ownership (Redwood / NovoThera):
- Network egress and NAT responsibility: NovoThera (we will validate routes and health checks)
- VPN / Interconnect: shared — Redwood will provide target endpoints and firewall rules to allow; NovoThera to provision on their side
- KMS & key residency: NovoThera-owned (customer-managed keys). Redwood will integrate via customer KMS connectors and will not store keys.
- Emergency access & break-glass: Redwood maintains documented break-glass runbook; emergency access will be initiated via a signed request and recorded in audit logs.
- Audit logs & retention: Redwood will stream inference and control-plane logs to the customer log sink for 90 days by default; extended retention options are available as an add-on.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Karthik: produce final network topology and minimal firewall rule set (by 2028-08-04).
2) Mina: confirm KMS connector checklist and required IAM roles (by 2028-08-05).
3) I will version the pledge file and circulate a DocuSign link once internal approvals complete (target 2028-08-06).

Attachments: redwood-pledge-draft.docx (Word, 45KB), networking-prereqs.md (text)

Let me know if you want this reviewed with your InfoSec — we can set a 30-minute slot early next week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@novothera.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Aug 2028 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment governance & access pledge for private deployment

Folks — sharing the network checklist and a draft topology for NovoThera's infra team. Highlights and a couple of required confirmations:

Network essentials (summary):
- IPingress: Customer to provide a /28 for tenant overlay plus NATing options. Redwood requires a stable public egress IP block for whitelisting and health probes.
- Allowed ports: 443 (TLS) outbound to Redwood endpoints, 5222 for optional agent telemetry (can be tunneled over 443), and a short list for KMS connector endpoints (provided in full in the attachment).
- MTU & path MTU: confirm 1500 vs jumbo frames — default 1500 recommended.
- Health checks: we will run TCP/HTTPS health checks every 15s from three regions; please confirm any internal firewall rate limits.

Attached: network-topology-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB) — this is a minimal topology showing transit, peering, and egress flow.

Two asks for NovoThera before we finalize the pledge:
1) Confirm the public egress IPs (or announceable prefix) you will use so we can pre-configure our routing policies.
2) Decide on KMS connectivity mode: (A) Private peered KMS endpoint via VPC peering or (B) Customer KMS with restricted public endpoints + mTLS. Option A has slightly lower latency but requires peering approvals.

If you want, I can hop on a short call Thursday to walk through the topology.

—Karthik
Senior Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@novothera.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Infra Team <infra-owner@novothera.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Aug 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment governance & access pledge for private deployment

Thanks, all. Reviewed the draft pledge and the topology — looks good. Our infra team confirmed the following:
- We will allocate a /28 for overlay and two stable egress IPs (eips@novothera.com provided a list in the separate ticket).
- We prefer KMS Option B (customer KMS with restricted endpoints + mTLS) to avoid peering approvals this sprint.
- Health-check frequency is acceptable; we'll whitelist Redwood probes.

I've attached the signed pledge (scanned) and added a few small clarifications to the KMS section; please confirm you are happy with the edits and I'll route the DocuSign envelope for final signatures today.

Attachments: signed-governance-pledge.pdf (PDF, 120KB), kms-ownership-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)

On the DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEFG-privdeploy — please review before I send.

Maria
Head of Infrastructure Programs
NovoThera Medical
